summary.status: Three completed critique/rebuttal rounds; no remaining blocking objection from Claude, with explicit Codex qualifications adopted.
summary.reviewer_scope: Claude read canonical JSON core sections at commit 09bd2ac, critique.txt and the repaired synthesis. It inspected the 18 project entries and 76 packages structurally, sampled stage examples/comparisons, and did not re-read all project reports, HTML, diagrams, ZIP or text/JSON parity. This is a document review, not a code audit.

rounds.purpose: All twelve decisions challenged against stages/contracts/roadmap/cost.
Codex rebutted invariants, cancellation, source scope, risk and measurement claims; Claude revised recommendations.
Final qualifications on processing gaps, conservative transmit markers, harmful restrictive instructions, risk assurance and attested values; Claude accepted them.

qualified_or_rejected: One event → one candidate: replaced with revision accounting and many-to-many evidence.
After claim means too late: replaced with fenced before-send marker, conservative unknown outcomes and verified cancellation.
Restrictive instructions are safe: rejected; delay, urgency and consequence remain part of risk.
Canaries alone establish rare-event recall: rejected; known-path tests and natural observations are reported separately.
Natural data alone is mandatory/sufficient for reliance: replaced with an authorized, risk-specific assurance case.
Rank or specificity silently overrides a hold: rejected; explicit override capability/target required.
Opening evidence proves review quality: rejected; use outcome-oriented review exercises and spot checks.
Every linked session has identical scope, or Gmail label selection is provider-enforced: unverified assumptions; inspect each adapter.
No electronic API means no usable evidence: qualified; dated authorized scans/counts/attestations can support limited checks.
A paid commitment must precede discovery: rejected; keep bounded discovery separate from demand and reliance gates.
summary.next_evidence: Actual code audit, permitted source access and real workflow observation. Another AI review cannot substitute for these.
summary.version_applied: Foundation 1.1 incorporates the Codex qualifications and final mechanism additions. Foundation 1.0 stays unchanged.

decisions.claude_objection: Router-declined messages can disappear from every board lane.
decisions.codex_response: Accept complete intake accounting; reject one message → one candidate and terminal-only counts.
decisions.accepted_change: Account for each source revision and workflow evaluation as pending, excluded with reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed events link to zero or more candidates; candidate matching and work status remain separate. Audit exclusions and replay changed rules.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Reconcile a fixed journal window including pending/failed items. One message creates several candidates; several messages support one candidate; an excluded critical item is found by independent review.

decisions.claude_objection: The authority system is named in prose, but external edits can invalidate pending decisions.
decisions.codex_response: Accept C17; observation is bounded by actual connector capability, not a promised universal one-sync guarantee.
decisions.accepted_change: Bind each authoritative field to a system, source identity/version or hash, read method, observation window, write mode and cutover. Revalidate the bound revision before admission/writeback; external changes stale dependent checks.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Edit a source while review is pending; require re-review. After cutover, conflicting edits to the former authority raise a dual-write exception.

decisions.claude_objection: An isolated parser may still hold broad database credentials and unrestricted egress.
decisions.codex_response: Accept worker profiles; differentiate untrusted parsers from trusted ingestion/effect services. Ordinary environment access is not itself a security failure.
decisions.accepted_change: Untrusted parser gets only the scoped asset, no production secrets or direct database access, restricted filesystem/egress, resource limits and a validated derivative-output API. Trusted workers receive separate least-privilege profiles.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Deny forbidden socket/filesystem/credential access; bound resource exhaustion; allow legitimate derivative submission and inspect quarantined failures.

decisions.claude_objection: A module name can be mistaken for tested implementation; evidence labels are templated.
decisions.codex_response: Accept commit-pinned audit rows and divergent entrypoints. Historical par/CC-224 cases are reproduction targets, not asserted fail/pass results.
decisions.accepted_change: Audit every H/C responsibility with commit, code path or explicit absence, entrypoints, known divergent paths and test artifacts. Distinguish not audited, absent, partial, present-untested and tested-at-commit.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Locate code and permitted fixtures; reproduce historical failures if available. A tested status requires pinned test evidence; the documentation template remains unfilled until then.

decisions.delivery_gate: Pilot / G1; review before runner expansion
decisions.claude_objection: A simple runner can grow into an unowned workflow engine.
decisions.codex_response: Accept a charter and owner; reject an arbitrary one-timer cap, quarterly-only review and automatic Temporal adoption.
decisions.accepted_change: Register job states, timer types and transitions. Support leases/fences, classified retries, outbox and scoped cancellation. Complex signal graphs, child orchestration or in-flight definition migration trigger a comparative engine spike. Domain effect reconciliation remains required.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Test crash, stale lease, timer, cancellation and upgrade recovery. Review complexity at phase exit and on new primitives or incidents; compare engineering and operating effort.

decisions.claude_objection: Selected groups may be a filter rather than a restriction at the provider.
decisions.codex_response: Accept source-enforced versus application-filtered distinctions; inspect the actual adapter instead of assuming all sessions or Gmail labels have identical scopes.
decisions.accepted_change: Disclose provider-visible scope and selected processing scope separately. Minimize nonselected content before durable capture, including controllable SDK cache/log/crash paths. Assess dedicated number/host, account risk and explicit exposure limits; reject incompatible deployments.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Inject nonselected content in a controlled test and inspect journal, media, traces, cache and crash artifacts. State measured exclusions and unavoidable session exposure; do not promise zero traces without evidence.

decisions.claude_objection: License checks miss protocol changes, provider terms and account restrictions.
decisions.codex_response: Accept an owner and fallback for external-service risks. Import success does not prove continuous capture.
decisions.accepted_change: Dependency records name provenance, rights, capabilities, provider/account constraints, failure owner and fallback mode with actual freshness limits. Only adopt what the chosen workflow needs.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Exercise selected connector recovery and a permitted import fallback; label manual/delayed operation and gaps rather than presenting it as live continuity.

decisions.claude_objection: Revocation, cancellation and a kill switch are underspecified once a request is in flight.
decisions.codex_response: Accept C06 policy/grant/epoch and cancellation evidence. Reject after claim = too late and atomic revocation across external systems.
decisions.accepted_change: Serialize local claims and durable before-send transmit markers with current grant/cancel epochs. A scope stop fences later boundaries. The marker means possible transmission, not success; earlier attempts may need reconciliation. Before-send prevention requires marker/fencing invariants on every path. Compensation is a new authorized action.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Inject revocation/cancel before claim, between claim/send, during send, after remote commit and after lost response. UI only claims prevented/cancelled/completed when evidence warrants it; otherwise unknown.

decisions.claude_objection: A blanket text-first launch could exclude evidence needed by the chosen photo/voice workflow.
decisions.codex_response: Accept required modalities per workflow; native-text-first is an extraction preference, not a product restriction. Video remains conditional on need.
decisions.accepted_change: C16 records required input modalities, language/noise conditions and citation locator types. Use native structure when suitable; process required images/voice from the first selected slice.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Score real permitted media by risk slice, wrong extraction and abstention. Show page/region/time locators where applicable and unsupported coverage explicitly.

decisions.delivery_gate: Pilot / G2; controls before rule activation
decisions.claude_objection: Instruction conflict, override, expiry and change-class authority are not explicit.
decisions.codex_response: Accept semantic fields; reject rank-plus-specificity as a universal override rule and shadow activation as sufficient proof for every high-risk change.
decisions.accepted_change: Use policy-defined override capabilities, explicit target/supersedes links and scope checks. Hold incompatible unresolved rules. Define timezone/boundary/condition/release authority. Confirmation policy depends on target/risk; ambiguous or consequential changes require exact review.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Cover owner hold versus subordinate release, ambiguous Friday, count-time thresholds, incompatible overlaps and action-in-flight supersession. Use replay/shadow plus protected future-case tests when risk requires.

decisions.delivery_gate: Pilot / G1 and every reliance expansion
decisions.claude_objection: Intake cannot be the sole source of its own eligible-event denominator.
decisions.codex_response: Accept independent inventories with provenance and known shared failure modes. Reject canaries as the only way to estimate rare-event recall or proof of natural-event recall.
decisions.accepted_change: C10 separates source observation basis, known gaps and processing coverage. C16 identifies independent inventory/eligibility adjudication and denominator status. Report labeled real-event results, synthetic/canary results and unknown unseen coverage separately. Record risk-slice reliance in C18; combine appropriately limited evidence in an authorized assurance case rather than requiring or trusting one evidence type universally.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Drop an event before intake and before routing; the comparison must detect or declare the unobservable gap. Live canaries require explicit consent and isolation from consequential workflows.

decisions.delivery_gate: Human roles when needed; automated delegation later
decisions.claude_objection: A CA or authorized operator may serve several businesses before agent exchange exists.
decisions.codex_response: Accept scoped human roles now; tenant boundaries alone are insufficient and cache clearing is not an authorization mechanism.
decisions.accepted_change: Give principals independent business/matter grants and explicit active context. Key caches by tenant, principal/grant revision and audience; recheck on reads. Cross-business disclosure is a separately authorized action, including for a common owner.
decisions.acceptance_or_revisit_test: Switch businesses, revoke one grant and reuse a stale context/cache key; no other business evidence is disclosed. Add automated agent exchange only after a repeated authorized workflow justifies it.
